title: Level 4 (Expert) - A-13
notes:
South should win the opening heart lead and cash 1 of dummy's top diamonds. 4 tricks in diamonds are needed (to go with 3 spades, 3 hearts, and 2 clubs). The early diamond play may reveal options in the suit.

West's play of the ♦9 gives South a 2 way finesse in diamonds. Either opponent may be played for 4 diamonds to the ♦J. West's play of the ♦9 from 4 diamonds to the ♦J is a well known mandatory falsecard. South should attempt to get a count on the hand to decide how to continue in diamonds.

In order to get as complete a count as possible, South should duck a round of clubs. When South regains the lead he can cash all of his tricks outside of diamonds. On the given lie of the cards, East will show up with 5 clubs and at least 3 cards in both spades and hearts. East will not have room for 4 diamonds in his hand. South will know to cash the ♦K next.

If the count does not reveal who to play for 4 diamonds, the odds favour playing a strong West player for length in diamonds and a weak West player for a singleton ♦9.
